tagline: The fjord-side capital where you can swim off the Opera House, metro to a ski jump, and meet the crowds that famously mobbed Speed.
overview: Oslo wraps a compact Nordic capital around the head of its own fjord. The Opera House's marble roof is a public slope you can walk on, the Munch museum holds The Scream, and the medieval Akershus fortress guards the harbour's mouth.

The city runs outdoors in every season: ferries to island beaches in summer, the metro to Nordmarka forest's ski jumps in winter, floating saunas on the harbour year-round. Vigeland Park's 200 granite sculptures stay open all night.
Speed's 2024 Europe stop became infamous — a crowd of fans mobbed him in the city centre in one of the tour's most-watched moments. Oslo has forgiven him; the fjord swims remain peaceful.

funFacts.title: A WALKABLE ROOF
funFacts.text: The Opera House's sloping marble roof is a public plaza — walk up it and sit on the roof.

funFacts.title: THE SCREAM'S HOME
funFacts.text: The Munch museum holds one version of The Scream; the National Museum has another.

funFacts.title: THE MOBBING
funFacts.text: Speed's 2024 Oslo stream was swarmed by fans — one of his most-watched clips ever.

funFacts.title: A FOREST METRO
funFacts.text: The metro climbs straight into Nordmarka wilderness — skis in winter, hikes in summer.

funFacts.title: 300-YEAR NAME CHANGE
funFacts.text: Oslo was called Christiania for three centuries before reclaiming its Norse name in 1925.

funFacts.title: SAUNA ON THE FJORD
funFacts.text: Floating wood-fired saunas let you steam, then plunge into the harbour.

funFacts.title: NOBEL CITY
funFacts.text: The Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo each December — the only Nobel given outside Sweden.

funFacts.title: A PARK OF PEOPLE
funFacts.text: Vigeland Park holds 200+ sculptures by one artist — free, around the clock.

funFacts.title: VIKING SHIPS
funFacts.text: The Viking Ship collection holds three of the world's best-preserved Viking vessels.

funFacts.title: ALMOST-MIDNIGHT SUN
funFacts.text: June nights barely darken — locals grill on the fjord at 11 p.m.
